study_name: DAYTRADE-002A: Early-to-Late Intraday Momentum Research Specification
hypothesis: Among a frozen universe of highly liquid U.S. market and sector ETFs, an unusually strong first-half-hour directional move predicts a same-direction return during the final half-hour of the same regular trading session that remains positive after realistic execution friction and exceeds comparable non-event sessions.
study_notes: Event-study methodology only; not an executable backtest. Simultaneous multi-ETF events on the same session date naturally occur and must be reported without suppression.

hypothesis_generation_disclosure.daytrade_001_reversal_status: development rejected, validation inconclusive, holdout unread_not_acquired
differences_from_daytrade_001: Signal horizon: 30-minute cumulative move (09:30-10:00 ET) vs 1-minute acute dislocation
Execution horizon: 15:30 open to 15:59 close vs next-minute open to next-minute close
Universe: 15 highly liquid market and sector ETFs vs 30 Dow single-stock equities
Timing: 10:00 ET signal availability with 5.5-hour information gap before 15:30 entry vs immediate next-minute entry
Mechanism: Information diffusion and end-of-day rebalancing continuation vs acute liquidity imbalance reversal
Dataset period: Fresh 2026 data vs 2025 data
hypothesis_generation_disclosure.no_reused_evidence_rule: No 2025 observations from DAYTRADE-001 development, validation, or holdout may serve as confirmatory evidence for DAYTRADE-002.

direction_notes: One symmetric directional hypothesis: LONG if first_half_hour_return > 0, SHORT if first_half_hour_return < 0. Long and short sides are reported separately as diagnostics, but the preregistered primary endpoint uses all qualifying signed events. No separate long/short promotion gates.

universe.name: SECTOR_ETFS
universe.source_of_truth_rule: The JSON symbol list is the research source of truth. The source preset is provenance only. Specification validity does not depend on future runtime preset values.
universe.universe_rationale: High-volume, highly liquid U.S. broad-market and SPDR sector ETFs with deep order books and minimal single-stock idiosyncratic risk.

dates_and_splits.split_adjacency_notes: Split boundaries are exchange-session aware under the XNYS calendar. Non-trading days (exchange holidays such as 2026-01-01 and calendar weekends) intervene between calendar dates without violating session adjacency.
dates_and_splits.holdout_access_rule: Holdout must remain unread, unparsed, unacquired, and uninspected unless validation earns exactly supported
dates_and_splits.locked_parameter_discipline: Parameters, percentiles, lookback windows, entry/exit rules, universes, costs, baseline definitions, and validation gates must not be modified after seeing development results.

session_semantics.minute_bar_timestamp_semantics: bar timestamp is the left edge of the one-minute interval
session_semantics.previous_close_reference: close of the 15:59 one-minute bar from the previous regular session

signal_definition.formula: first_half_hour_return(i, D) = (close(i, D, 09:59 bar) / close(i, previous_regular_session, 15:59 bar)) - 1
signal_definition.previous_close_reference: close of the 15:59 one-minute bar from the previous regular session

threshold_definition.history_scope: previous 20 valid completed regular sessions for that ticker (excluding current session D)
history_rules: excluded/invalid sessions do not count toward the 20 valid sessions
calendar days cannot substitute for valid sessions

event_definition.simultaneous_events: Cross-ETF simultaneous events on the same session date are naturally permitted and tracked without suppression.

timing.exit_semantics_notes: The 15:59 bar close is the closing price of the one-minute interval [15:59:00, 16:00:00); it is not assumed to equal the official closing-auction or daily close.
timing.prohibited_intervening_information_use: no information from 10:00 ET through the 15:30 entry may be used to alter event eligibility, direction, entry eligibility, or sizing

primary_endpoint.name: final_half_hour_return_30m
primary_endpoint.algebraic_equivalence: sign * (exit / entry - 1) where sign is +1 for LONG and -1 for SHORT
primary_endpoint.session_boundary_rule: Fills must not cross 16:00 regular-session boundary

matched_baseline.description: For each event observation, compare against qualifying non-event sessions for the same ticker, same split, and same first-half-hour direction.
matched_baseline.reference_return_formula: arithmetic mean of all qualifying matched non-event signed net returns
matched_baseline.empty_baseline_rule: If no qualifying baseline observations exist, baseline is non_computable, uplift is non_computable; never substitute zero.

statistical_inference.rationale: 15 ETFs share common market shocks and multiple ETF signals on the same day are cross-sectionally dependent.
algorithm_steps: 1. Sample eligible target-split session dates with replacement
2. Preserve all ticker observations from each sampled session
3. Preserve multiplicity when a date is sampled more than once
5. Recompute matched baseline using resampled observations
statistical_inference.joint_recomputation_rule: Baseline is not held fixed; joint uncertainty is evaluated across both event and baseline distributions
statistical_inference.non_computable_rule: If a required replicate statistic is non-computable, entire relevant CI status = non_computable; do not drop replicate, do not substitute zero, do not reduce denominator.

step_1_invalidity.condition: Methodological or data-integrity failures, including: lookahead or future leakage, premature holdout access, material timestamp or execution invalidity, split contamination, silent provider or feed substitution, or corrupt/unverifiable inputs.

step_2_evidence_sufficiency.condition: Otherwise valid, but any evidence-sufficiency condition fails: fewer than 75 eligible events, fewer than 10 represented ETFs, fewer than 20 distinct event session dates, single-ETF event concentration > 15.0%, or > 5.0% excluded ticker-sessions in split due to data-quality defects. Holdout must not be inspected.

step_3_directional_hypothesis_failure.condition: Adequate and valid evidence, but any of the following directional failures occur: primary mean net return at 2 bps/side <= 0; mean event-minus-baseline uplift <= 0; or fewer than 60.0% of represented ETFs have positive primary mean net return (breadth gate failure).

step_4_statistical_uncertainty.condition: Required means are positive and breadth passes (>= 60%), but either required 95% CI lower bound is <= 0 (primary net return CI lower bound <= 0 OR uplift CI lower bound <= 0), or a required CI is non-computable.

step_5_support.condition: All six locked gates pass simultaneously on the evaluated split.

disposition_precedence.holdout_application: The exact same 5-step disposition sequence and precedence rules apply to conditional holdout evaluation.

literature_references.citation: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018), Market Intraday Momentum, Journal of Financial Economics
Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka (2010), Intraday Patterns in the Cross-section of Stock Returns, Journal of Finance
Rosa (2022), Understanding Intraday Momentum Strategies, Journal of Futures Markets

explicit_out_of_scope: reusing or modifying the DAYTRADE-001 evaluator
alternative percentiles, lookback windows, or return definitions
